riley: Running a longctx sim (8k) on INT8 kernels; seeing gradual memory growth even after expected evictions. BF16 run is stable. Perf profile attached. Anyone else see reuse degradation after ~2k tokens?

alex: can you paste the perf output? curious about slab churn and slot counts.

riley: here's the quick perf snippet I grabbed: ```
# perf_top --filter=kv_cache --period=50ms
kv_slot_alloc: +42%
slab_coalesce: -10%
page_faults: +3/rate
```

sam: that +42% kv_slot_alloc smells like fragmentation -> not reclaiming free slots. Did you run compaction/passive reclaim?

riley: compaction is enabled (threshold=0.15). I lowered it to 0.05 and saw less growth but INT8 runs showed a small accuracy delta (~0.8% drop on our rerank eval after warmup: 84.2 -> 83.4).

morgan: accuracy drop could be quantization + warmup gaps. Another angle: are we switching kernel variants on page load? if a page is evicted and reloaded we might pick a different kernel/quant path.

riley: yes, kernel selection currently does: ```select_kernel(model, page->precision) -> if page_resident then INT8_OPT else FALLBACK_BF16``` so reloads can land on fallback.

alex: propose experiment: pin INT8_OPT for pages classified as hot (hit_count > 50) and increase prefetch window. Also emit telemetry per page: kv_page_age, last_kernel, hit_count.

sam: ran a quick local with INT8 pin + prefetch=32: reduced mem growth from +120MB -> +18MB across 10k tokens; p95 latency +3ms. Accuracy delta improved to +0.1% vs BF16. CLI I used: ```./run_sim --prefetch=32 --pin-hot-kernel```

riley: that's promising. can we roll a canary to dedicated and include the rerank eval after warmup? also need to monitor long-term INT8 noise per @eng-sre.

devops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-eng-runtime/kvcache-int8-pin at 2024-05-22T14:00Z

morgan: also add a derived eviction metric kv_fragment_ratio = holes/slots. if >0.3 trigger compaction and consider slab-compact singleflight to avoid oscillation.

riley: TODOs: add telemetry (kv_page_age, last_kernel, hit_count, kv_fragment_ratio), run canary on dedicated, include eval-runpost to catch quality regressions, tweak compaction thresholds, and document kernel pin heuristic. thx :thumbsup:
